items.title: Getting Started: build Compass
items.description: Build Compass on Copilotz 1.0: import the agentic core, rebuild Copilotz's other plugins for one person, one primitive at a time.

items.title: Ch 1: One agent, one message
items.description: Compose a runtime from two of Copilotz's plugins and one of your own, send an agent a message, and read the events it leaves.

items.title: Ch 2: North, in your terminal
items.description: Move North into a plugin of your own, laid out by primitive; give the team a charter as a View in North's prompt; talk to North in Copilotz's terminal and see exactly what it's sent.

items.title: Ch 3: Compass in the browser
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's identity plugin for one person on their own machine (a collection, an Action, a who, a route and a rule), then serve Compass's web page in its own look.

items.title: Ch 4: Today, every turn
items.description: Tell every agent today's date with a turn context, and see why a prompt has a stable part and a part that changes: the provider's prompt cache.

items.title: Ch 5: One store
items.description: Keep Compass in one SQLite file: what the store's tables hold, each collection as a SQL view, and why the store has one writer at a time.

items.title: Ch 6: Chats that name themselves
items.description: Write a Processor: it hears chat's message.created events and names new chats with a small model. Then test it with a scripted model, swapped in through resources and an adapter.

items.title: Ch 7: Spaces
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's spaces plugin for one person by its contract: what chat and other plugins ask of it, a rule that keeps shared documents in real spaces, and a parity test against Copilotz's own.

items.title: Ch 8: Spaces on the web
items.description: Give spaces a web front end: React Views the web shell places by name, a page for each space, and resource kinds that let other plugins add tabs without knowing your code.

items.title: Ch 9: The board's data and Actions
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's boards: two collections that must always agree, seven Actions that are the only way to change them, and transactions that commit what several documents must agree on together.

items.title: Ch 10: The board on screen
items.description: Show the same board in two places with Views: a Board tab on every space's page, plugged in through a resource kind, and a terminal View printed by a command. Both stay live.

items.title: Ch 11: The board for North
items.description: The third place the board shows is the model's prompt: six tools, offered wherever a conversation is in a space, that call the same Actions people use, and read back as plain text.

items.title: Ch 12: Documents and their versions
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's documents plugin for one person by its contract: Markdown in a space, every save a version that says who, what and when, an old version brought back as a new one, and a stale save refused.

items.title: Ch 13: Saves that merge, or refuse
items.description: Two saves from the same version merge line by line, a three-way merge against the version both started from, and are refused only where they touch the same lines; and who has a document open is live, in a collection kept in memory.

items.title: Ch 14: Documents on the web and in the terminal
items.description: The same documents shown by Views in two places: a Documents tab on every space, a page to write and save each version, live as others save, and /doc in the terminal.

items.title: Ch 15: Documents for North
items.description: Documents' third reader is the model: five tools, offered wherever a conversation is in a space, that read and write through the same commit as your saves, each change a version by the agent, for you.

items.title: Ch 16: A line for every message
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's history plugin, starting with its Processor: as messages leave the recent tail, each gets a line, and pairs of lines merge up a binary tree, with a cheap model only for what's long.

items.title: Ch 17: The outline in North's prompt
items.description: Replace chat's history View: an agent is sent the summary lines first, then the recent messages whole, and chat reads only those, from where the history plugin says they start.

items.title: Ch 18: Zoom
items.description: A summary line never replaces its messages: the zoom tool, offered once a thread is summarized, opens a line into the two it was made from, down to the message itself, whole.

items.title: Ch 19: Memories found by meaning
items.description: Rebuild the store half of Copilotz's memory plugin: statements about a person, an agent, a conversation or everyone, kept with an embedding, found by meaning and by words, and updated instead of repeated.

items.title: Ch 20: Recall in the prompt
items.description: Memory reaches agents as three of chat's contexts: how to use it in the cached system part, the core memories when a conversation begins, and each turn the memories relevant to what was last said.

items.title: Ch 21: Remember, recall, forget
items.description: Three tools with Copilotz's names and inputs let agents keep, search and drop memories; the charter says what's worth keeping, and the terminal and the web show what's kept.

items.title: Ch 22: Memories on their own
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's memoryExtraction: a Processor counts each conversation's shared messages and, every few, asks a cheap model to write down what's worth keeping, through the same keep as remember.

items.title: Ch 23: East, South and West
items.description: North gets a team: three more of the app's own agents, each with its own way of working and its own model alias, in every space, with the charter in each one's prompt.

items.title: Ch 24: Asking in parallel
items.description: North brings teammates in with chat's send_message: questions that don't depend on each other go out in one step, the teammates work at the same time, and North resumes once, with every reply.

items.title: Ch 25: Reading other conversations
items.description: Compass's coordination plugin, rebuilt for one person: two tools that let an agent list and read the other conversations of its space, through chat's own queries, storing nothing.

items.title: Ch 26: Skills
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's skills plugin for one person: know-how an agent reads only when a task calls for it, listed by name in the cached part of its prompt and read with one tool.

items.title: Ch 27: Routines on a schedule
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's routines for one person: a message sent to an agent on a schedule, with time as one more caller of Actions, every run recorded, and tests that move time with a manual clock.

items.title: Ch 28: Agents that schedule
items.description: \"Remind me every Monday\" from a chat: four tools that make, list and cancel routines as the person the agent works for, post back where they were asked, and let an agent name a run's chat for what it found.

items.title: Ch 29: Search, an adapter port
items.description: Rebuild Copilotz's web tools for one person, starting with web_search: a tool that knows no search engine and asks an adapter port, so DuckDuckGo, Serper or an offline fake answers, all through the runtime's fetch.

items.title: Ch 30: Reading a page safely
items.description: read_page fetches a page an agent chose and hands back its main text, marked as data: http(s) only, private and metadata addresses refused on every redirect, within a time, a size and a kind of content, and a few pages per turn.

items.title: Ch 31: Fakes at the edges
items.description: Test Compass as a person uses it, offline and in milliseconds: the app as app.ts makes it, run for real, with fakes only where it meets the world: a scripted model, a manual clock, and a model provider served on your machine.

items.title: Ch 32: Parity
items.description: What every rebuilt plugin's parity test does, in one small helper: the same scenario on Copilotz's plugin and on yours, with ids and times taken out; and the parity test identity was missing, with testWho saying who each request is.

items.title: Ch 33: The REST API
items.description: Other programs reach Compass: the runtime answers /api/ itself, as whoever identity's who says a request is, so a script on your machine reads your board and moves a card through the same Actions and rules as a click.

items.title: Ch 34: The client
items.description: Copilotz's client, connect, reaches the running server as plugin code reaches the store, over the socket or over HTTP; its watch hears every commit, so a script prints your board again whenever a card moves.

items.title: Ch 35: Your board over MCP
items.description: An assistant on your machine (Claude Code, any MCP client) calls the board's tools, the same ones North uses: Compass's own mcp plugin, with Copilotz's contract, for one person, each call written in a chat of yours.

items.title: Ch 36: PostgreSQL and blobs
items.description: Run the same Compass on PostgreSQL when DATABASE_URL says so, and keep large values once, as files in a folder of their own, with Copilotz's postgresStore and fileBlobs.

items.title: Ch 37: Watching it run
items.description: Copilotz measures itself: the runtime's jobs and commits, and every model call by OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions. Give it a meter, read the numbers at /metrics as Prometheus text or in the terminal, and send them to an OpenTelemetry collector.

items.title: Ch 38: A computer for your agents
items.description: Run Copilotz's computers plugin, unchanged, on Compass's spaces: a machine you connect with a one-time code, where North gets a terminal, jobs, files, a browser and web search, and asks before it runs anything. One change to spaces makes it fit: you are a member of your spaces, the way Copilotz's keep it.

items.title: Ch 39: Swapping in Copilotz's plugins
items.description: Every plugin you rebuilt kept Copilotz's contract, so one setting runs Compass on Copilotz's own plugins instead, the real Compass's. A test runs the same end-to-end scenario on both lists, and shows where they differ on purpose.

items.title: Ch 40: Sign-in and people
items.description: On Copilotz's identity, a request is whoever its session proves, so people sign in: by email and a password, with codes written to the log on this machine, or by name. Then a space gets members: Ana invites Bruno to Launch, he accepts, and he reads its board.

items.title: Ch 41: Many orgs and billing
items.description: One address, many orgs: a directory runtime signs people in and knows their orgs, and each org is a Compass of its own, opened when used and closed when idle. With Copilotz's usage ledger, what each org's agents use is recorded and priced in that org alone.
